title: FreeCAD to OpenStudio floorplan exchange
description: Output of fc_export_floorplan.py, input to build_osm_geometry.py and update_osm_geometry.py. All lengths are metres. Hand-authoring this file is supported; the only field that must be preserved across edits is each space's id.

schema_version.description: 1 is a flat-topped plan. 2 may also carry a roof, the per-space solids it produces, and the story an attic invents. 3 may also carry air_boundary_overrides. 4 lets an ordinary (non-roofed) room's walls be pre-split and pre-paired at their true 2D wall-centerline network + per-room height, the same way a roof's attic floor/ceiling mirror pairs already were, via a `solid` block synthesized directly instead of only from a roof. Every earlier version's plan is a valid later-version plan; the reverse is not true, so a reader that does not understand a field new to a later version must refuse rather than build the wrong model by accident.

source_document.description: Basename of the FCStd this came from.

units.description: Present so a future imperial variant cannot be misread.

north_axis_deg.description: OS:Building North Axis. Geometry is drawn relative to plan north.

roof.description: Present only when the document declares a roof. Schema version 2.

air_boundary_overrides.description: Hand-made SOLID/OPEN declarations, tagged in FreeCAD directly on a wall-centerline edge (tag_airboundary.FCMacro) rather than named against a previously built OpenStudio surface. Re-derived fresh on every export, so the drawing stays the source of truth across a full rebuild. Schema version 3.

elevation_m.description: Floor elevation. Negative means below grade, which makes the builder flip that story's exterior walls to Ground.

floor_to_floor_m.description: Height every space on this story is extruded to, unless it carries its own height_m.

source_sketch.description: Internal FreeCAD object name of the sketch, for traceability. Absent on a story the roof invented rather than a sketch, which carries source_object instead.

source_object.description: Internal FreeCAD object name of the roof solid that produced this story. Marks an attic story: it has no plan sketch and no room labels, so nothing that accounts for labels should count its spaces.

id.description: Stable UUID, held as OS_SpaceId on the room's Draft Text label. Change propagation matches on this and nothing else, so it must never be regenerated for an existing room.

area_m2.description: Computed by FreeCAD. The builder checks the OpenStudio space against this and fails past 0.1%.

height_m.description: Optional per-room override of the story's floor_to_floor_m, for a double-height lobby or a bay open to the roof. Held as OS_Height_m on the room's label, where 0 means defer. Omitted whenever the room defers, so its presence marks a deliberate decision; it also joins the change-propagation hash only when present, leaving deferring rooms hashing as they did before this field existed.

vertices.description: Wall-centerline polygon, counter-clockwise in plan, no repeated closing vertex, collinear runs already collapsed. z comes from the story elevation, not from here.

solid.description: Present when the roof gave this space a shape a prism cannot describe, or (schema 4) when an ordinary room's walls were pre-split and pre-paired against its 2D neighbours instead of being left to intersectSurfaces. When it is here it is the geometry: vertices and height_m still describe the footprint and are still what the area check and the space-matching use, but they no longer say what gets built.
A space stated as an explicit closed set of faces rather than as a floor print plus a height.

source.description: Which method produced this. roof-extend raised an existing room to meet the roof; roof-attic is the roof solid itself, become a space; wall-network (schema 4) is an ordinary room whose walls were pre-split and pre-paired against its 2D neighbours (fc_walls.py) instead of being left to intersectSurfaces.

roof_object.description: Internal FreeCAD object name of the roof, for traceability.

type.description: What FreeCAD made of the outward normal. OpenStudio derives this itself from the winding and is the authority; the builder compares the two and reports any disagreement, because disagreement means a face is wound inside out.

vertices.description: Closed polygon in metres, no repeated closing vertex, wound counter-clockwise seen from outside the space so the normal points away from it. Unlike a space's plan vertices these carry z, and it is absolute model elevation, not a height above the story.

match_id.description: Opaque per-build correlation key: two surfaces sharing one are the same physical boundary and are paired with setAdjacentSurface before intersectSurfaces runs. Not stable across exports/builds; never written to the .osm.

match_space_id.description: OS_SpaceId of the room this surface's match_id is expected to pair with. Present on a wall-network pre-pair; a roof-mirror pair may omit it.

air_boundary_override.description: One tagged wall-centerline edge, resolved at export time to the pair of rooms it separates and its own plan line -- never to an OpenStudio surface name, which is positional and does not survive a full rebuild.

kind.description: SOLID: real construction (a fire wall, a rated separation), overriding any rule that would otherwise flag this wall as an air boundary. OPEN: force an air boundary here, overriding any rule.

space_a.description: OS_SpaceId of the room on one side of the tagged edge.

space_b.description: OS_SpaceId of the room on the other side.

vertices.description: The tagged edge's two endpoints, metres, same plan frame as a space's own vertices. Used to find the built surface(s) by position after intersectSurfaces may have split the wall, and to disambiguate when the same pair of rooms shares more than one wall.

roof.description: What the document's roof objects did. Reporting, not instruction: the geometry itself lives in each space's solid, so a consumer that ignores this block still builds the right model.

method.description: Extend raised the spaces below to meet the roof. Attic made the roof a space of its own and turned the ceilings below it into interior surfaces. The choice is an energy question -- whether the roof construction faces conditioned air directly or across an unconditioned buffer.

base_elevation_m.description: Lowest point of the roof. A space is extended when its ceiling sits within tolerance of this.

area_m2.description: Sloped area of the upward-facing roof faces -- the loss surface.

plan_area_m2.description: Its shadow. area_m2 over this is the price of the pitch, and on a low-slope roof it is a fraction of a percent.

extended.description: One entry per space the Extend method reshaped.

attics.description: One entry per Attic roof, each of which became a space.
